newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghana's Rawlings within sight of historic poll win.
newsitem.headline: Ghana's Rawlings within sight of historic poll win.

text.p: President Jerry Rawlings, who has dominated national life in Ghana for almost two decades, was within sight of a historic election victory on Tuesday as the first incumbent to be re-elected since independence in 1957.
Only a late surge by John Kufuor of the opposition's Great Alliance could force the race into a second round.
"Rawlings widens gap," the influential Daily Graphic said in its main headline on Tuesday. Election officials said they expected to issue final results later in the day.

With passions running high, an election commissioner said a mob jostled him near the opposition stronghold of Kumasi, capital of the pre-colonial Ashanti empire, after seeing him with a ruling party parliamentary candidate.
With results in from 139 of the 200 constituencies in Saturday's presidential and parliamentary elections, Rawlings enjoyed a comfortable lead with 54 percent of votes.

His main challenger, Kufuor had 43.7 percent, according to the results from the National Election Commission. The third contender, surgeon Edward Mahama of the People's National Convention, trailed with below 2.3 percent of votes.
Rawlings, a charismatic former air force pilot, twice seized power in the West African nation. He ruled unchallenged for 15 years before first winning a popular mandate in 1992.
Since independence from Britain, all Ghana's elected governments have been toppled before serving out their terms.
In the parliamentary ballot, the president's National Democratic Congress party had 88 seats in the 200-seat assembly. The combined opposition had 51 seats.

The election commission put turnout at about 80 percent in the elections praised by foreign poll observers as among the best organised in a region where logistics problems have marred voting in recent elections, often leading to violence.
"This is by far the best organised election I have seen in West Africa," one Western monitor said.
Commonwealth and Organisation of African Unity observers have paid tribute to the conduct of the elections.
Despite tension and some violence in the runup to voting, polling day itself passed off smoothly.

Kufuor, who celebrated his 58th birthday on Sunday, has said he would congratulate Rawlings if it emerged he was the winner. "If this trend continues and I lose I will respect the traditional way," he told Reuters on Sunday.
Rawlings seized power as an air force flight-lieutenant in 1979, executing three former heads of state. He restored civilian rule but seized power again in 1981.
A former socialist firebrand, he embraced Western-style free-market economics, winning plaudits from the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

The main opposition went into the 1992 elections in disarray and boycotted the 1992 parliamentary poll. Against the odds, Kufuor's New Patriotic Party and the People's Convention Party (PCP) formed a common front for this year's elections.
The PCP, which did not exist in 1992, follows the socialist line promoted by Kwame Nkrumah, Ghana's first president.
The Ghana Stock Exchange recorded one of its largest recent falls on Monday but brokers said it had nothing to do with the elections but rather someone wanting to sell at all costs.
"It shows how young our market is. It needs only one person cashing in for Christmas to lower the GSE All-Share Index by over five points," said Keli Gadzekpo of stockbrokers Databank.
